name: Paid election worker (municipal, provincial or federal elections)
summary: Short-term paid jobs staffing voting places for municipal, provincial or federal elections; hiring happens in the weeks or months before each vote.
what_you_do: After a short paid training session, you work at a voting location on advance-poll days or election day, greeting voters, checking registration, issuing ballots or supervising. Days often run 12-14 hours, and the election office decides your assignment.
who_it_may_fit: You want occasional, short, in-person paid work, can handle long days and can stay politically neutral.
Paid training (Elections Canada pays about 3 hours)
No experience needed for entry roles
Elections Canada accepts online applications at any time; age 16+ for federal elections
Ontario municipal examples: $225-$300/day plus $50-$60 for training in Windsor-Essex (news); Toronto lists about $280 for one role
Often assigned near your home
who_it_may_not_fit: You need regular income or remote work, or cannot manage a 13-14 hour day on site.
Very long days (12-14 hours) on site
Work exists only around elections, so it is sporadic
Toronto's hiring for the October 26, 2026 municipal election is closed (positions filled); other cities' training ran late September-early October, so this cycle is likely too late
Must stay non-partisan; candidates, their families and campaign workers are excluded
Eligibility differs: federal requires Canadian citizenship and age 16+; Toronto requires 18+ and legal right to work
Federal pay rates differ between Elections Canada pages and years; check the current rate

conditions_notes: Only during election periods; next federal/provincial dates depend on when elections are called.
Mandatory training; Elections Canada pays about 3 hours; Toronto training about 2.5 hours; Windsor-Essex pays $50-$60.

economics_notes: Varies by election and role. Elections Canada pages: roughly $20-$27/hr (one page), $27.76 for central poll supervisor (another); 2025 news: $17.40-$33.08/hr. Ontario municipal 2026 examples: $225-$300/day (Windsor-Essex news), about $280 (Toronto).

name: Registered apprenticeship in a skilled trade (Ontario)
summary: Earn-while-you-learn route into a skilled trade: you work for a sponsor and register a training agreement with Skilled Trades Ontario.
what_you_do: Most of your time is paid, on-the-job work under qualified tradespeople, with time off for in-school technical training. You hold a registered training agreement and carry a Registered Apprentice Wallet Card while working.
who_it_may_fit: You like hands-on, physical work and want to be paid while you train toward a trade.
Paid while you learn; sponsors must follow Ontario law, including minimum wage
No special course or school enrolment needed to start; the key step is finding a sponsor
Sponsors can be employers, journeypersons, contractors, unions or industry associations
Online portal (or paper) application; training done in another province can be recognized after verification
who_it_may_not_fit: You need remote work, or you cannot yet find an employer or other sponsor to take you on.
You must find a sponsor in Ontario before you can register, which can be the hardest step
Minimum age 16, legal permission to work in Canada, and trade-specific education requirements
Trades with ratios need a 1:1 journeyperson-to-apprentice ratio, limiting how many apprentices an employer can take
Mostly physical, on-site work; length of apprenticeship and classroom fees not checked here

conditions_notes: Depends on the sponsor's workload and trade.
In-school technical training is part of the apprenticeship; classroom fees and grants not verified.

economics_notes: Paid by the sponsor; Skilled Trades Ontario says sponsors must comply with minimum wage laws. Trade-specific rates not checked.

name: Government student and new-grad job programs (FSWEP, Ontario SEO, Ontario Internship Program)
summary: Federal and Ontario public-service hiring streams reserved for students (FSWEP, Ontario Summer Employment Opportunities) and recent graduates (Ontario Internship Program).
what_you_do: You submit a profile or applications to a government student inventory or job board; departments and ministries hire students for temporary jobs (often summer, sometimes part-time during the school year) or recent grads for internships. Work ranges from office and program support to field jobs such as natural-resources roles.
who_it_may_fit: You are a full-time student or recent Ontario grad who wants paid government work experience.
FSWEP is the federal government's largest student hiring program, open to full-time high-school, college and university students returning to studies
FSWEP part-time roles possible during the school year; full-time in breaks
Ontario SEO hires up to about 4,000 students for 7-18 week full-time summer jobs; 2027 postings expected in fall/winter
Ontario Internship Program is for recent college/university grads (within 2 years; 5 years for bilingual, Indigenous or disabled candidates); recruitment begins in December
Government work experience for your resume
who_it_may_not_fit: You are not a student or recent grad, or you need work immediately this autumn.
Student status required (FSWEP: full-time and returning next term)
Being in the FSWEP inventory does not guarantee a referral; departments search the pool
Ontario SEO 2026 ads are closed and OIP applications are currently closed (ontario.ca)
SEO requires living in Ontario during the job, age 15+ (some roles 18+), legal right to work and a SIN
International-student eligibility for FSWEP only claimed by a third-party guide; unverified
A 2019-20 PSC audit found departments saw FSWEP rules as inflexible and some referrals were bypassed

requirements.education: current student status (FSWEP, SEO) or recent degree/diploma (OIP)

name: Temporary placements through staffing agencies (office/admin and general)
summary: Licensed temp and staffing agencies (e.g., Randstad, Adecco, Robert Half) place workers in short-term or contract roles, including office and admin work that is occasionally partly remote.
what_you_do: You register with one or more agencies, talk with a recruiter, and get offered assignments at client companies such as reception, office support, data entry or industrial roles. Assignments can last from days to months, and some can turn into permanent jobs.
who_it_may_fit: You want to start earning soon in short-term office or general roles and do not mind changing assignments.
Can lead to work quickly; temp roles often open and close within 48 hours (Randstad)
In Ontario, temp help agencies cannot charge workers fees for becoming an agency employee or being assigned work
Ontario requires temporary help agencies and recruiters to be licensed (O. Reg. 99/23)
Some admin postings are hybrid (e.g., a Randstad admin role remote except one office day a week)
who_it_may_not_fit: You need guaranteed steady hours or only fully remote work.
Fully remote temp admin work appears sporadic; most listings found were on-site
Assignment-based work means hours and income can be uneven
Many postings are tied to one city (e.g., Greater Montreal only)
Fake recruiters impersonate agencies; verify the agency and never pay a fee
Agencies' own job-seeker terms were not verified in this pass

conditions_notes: Assignment-based; remote admin openings appear sporadic in search results.

economics_notes: Pay varies by assignment; not checked.

who_it_may_fit: You are comfortable making many phone calls to strangers and want a government job that may be done from home.

Federal employer; clerks may be eligible for Public Service group insurance benefit plans

Ontario median wage for survey interviewers and statistical clerks is about $24.18/hr (Job Bank, all employers)
who_it_may_not_fit: You dislike phone work or rejection, or you need guaranteed full-time hours.
Hiring is 'as needed'; no current Ontario posting was confirmed
Phone-heavy: lots of calls to strangers, some of whom assume it is a scam (worker reviews)
Hours up to 35/week; reviewers say many roles are part-time

A reported posting required reliable home phone service and willingness to travel
